messages:
Sam (product): Quick sync request  Pilot banks want a hard acceptance checklist before we flip Dedicated for them. They called out: tamper-evidence, per-tenant retention lanes, key rotation that doesn't break verification, and an ops playbook for legal holds/escape paths. Need alignment on MUST vs MAY for MVP.
Jules (eng-plat): From a platform POV the smallest useful surface is: export API, manifest with per-file sha256, a signer_id+key_version in manifest, and a signed envelope (AsymmetricSign). We can include optional RFC3161 timestamping if legal wants a timestamp token. Implementation fast-path: no merkle in MVP to keep CPU/e2e simpler.
Rina (security): Rotation/back-compat is the tricky bit. Requirement: exports signed before rotation must remain verifiable. Option A: tenants retain their old public keys and upload them to Console. Option B: we store tenant public-key history (encrypted-at-rest) and publish a signed key timeline that maps key_versions -> validity windows. We'll need a revocation list flow too.
Marco (ops): Operational constraints: full indexing for 7y is not feasible for all customers. Must offer retention tiers: hot (90d, sub-5s), warm (1-2y, sub-30s), cold (up to 7y, retrieval SLA 24-72h). Suggest making long-term indexing an opt-in paid feature. Also exports are heavy; queue + rate-limit with rush lane paid option.
Sam (product): Proposed acceptance checklist for pilot (MUST): 1) Signed export manifest (per-file checksums + signer+key_version). 2) Retention lanes with opt-in billing for long-term indexing. 3) Legal-hold toggle that blocks purge jobs. 4) Key rotation policy that preserves verification. 5) Export audit events and proof-of-delivery. MAY: RFC3161 timestamping, merkle proofs, HSM attestation UI.
Jules (eng-plat): Dev notes: manifest prototype fields: format, files[], signer, key_version, signature, generated_at. Eg:
```json
{"format":"tar.gz","files":[{"path":"audit.log","sha256":"..."}],"signer":"projects/redwood-kms/keys/t-77/versions/3","key_version":"3","signature":"BASE64...","generated_at":"2026-03-23T12:00:00Z"}
```
We will add a `verification_token` field later for Console checks. Timeline: 2 sprints for core export+signing+retention plumbing, +1 sprint for Console verification UX.
Rina (security): Verification UX must let customers upload archived public keys and run a one-click verify which checks signature -> key_version -> per-file sha256. Audit events: export_requested, export_generated, signature_verified, verification_failed. Also require signed proof-of-delivery (receipt) we store and return.
Marco (ops): Runbook sketch: request -> auth & billing check -> enqueue -> snapshot -> create manifest -> sign -> store artifact -> produce signed receipt -> notify tenant. Include concurrent export caps, max export size, and emergency "escape hatch" flow requiring dual approval. SLA proposal for pilot: small exports (<10GB) <24h, large best-effort; paid rush lane target <6h.
contracts-bot: Legal: add SLA appendix for evidence availability and an emergency-release clause (escape hatch). Recommend pilot warranty: 30-day evidence delivery guarantee. We'll draft template with limits and dual-approval requirement for emergency releases.
Sam (product): We also need QA tests for verification. QA-bot, can you list verification test cases?
QA-bot: Quick list: 1) verify-signature-with-current-key, 2) verify-signature-with-archived-key (post-rotation), 3) verify-manifest-file-hash-mismatch detection, 4) verify-legal-hold blocks purge, 5) emergency-release requires dual-approval and emits release token, 6) export-size and rate-limit enforcement.
Sam (product): Nice. Pricing question: Marco, please produce cost delta for offering warm-index vs cold-only for 2y data. We need numbers for PRD.
Marco (ops): Will do. Roughs now: hot index ~ $0.025/GB/mo, warm ~ $0.008/GB/mo, cold archive ~ $0.001/GB/mo + retrieval fees. Will model per-tenant opt-ins and a paid rush export fee.
Jules (eng-plat): One more engineering note: for BYOK we can support two modes: 1) tenant provides public key (we sign using their KMS via AsymmetricSign RPC or they sign themselves), 2) tenants upload PEM public keys and we call Redwood HSM as fallback (with HSM attestation recorded). We'll document recommended default = tenant-managed KMS.
Rina (security): I'll produce a rotation & revocation policy doc: how we record key_version, timeline for key validity, how revocations are published, and UX for customers to upload archived keys.
Sam (product): Action items recap: Jules -> manifest prototype + sample CLI; Rina -> rotation & revocation policy; Marco -> cost model + ops runbook; contracts -> SLA + emergency-release clause; QA-bot -> test matrix. I'll pull into a 1-page PRD and book 30m decision sync tomorrow. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
